To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a tight bound on the probability of peak power of OFDM signal can be obtained from the oversampled signal; (2) the probability of the peak power of an OFDM system can be computed using a simple closed form expression; and (3) the peak power can be accurately estimated using the oversampled inverse FFT or the minimum distance decoding method.

the peak power of OFDM can be tightly bounded by the maximum of the corresponding oversampled sequence, which can be computed efficiently, and the peak-to-average ratio of uncoded signals can be tightly upper bounded by a closed-form expression.

(a) a new bound for peak envelope of OFDM signals is introduced based on oversampling and is very tight for large oversampling rates, (b) a closed-form probability bound is derived for the complementary cumulative density function of the peak to mean power ratio of uncodes OFDM signals, (c) relative errors in peak power computation are derived for two methods of computing the peak power.

the problem of peak power estimation in OFDM signals.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oversampling can be very useful for peak power computation of OFDM signals.

, for uncoded OFDM, the oversampling method is the most efficient method in terms of computational complexity and accuracy for the computation of the peak-to-average ratio of the continuous envelope, and the oversampled inverse FFT is the most efficient for the computation of peak-to-average power ratio of the discrete envelope.
the oversampling rate has to be chosen high enough, but not too high, for accurate peak power estimation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the peak-to-mean power ratio of OFDM signals can be tightly upper bounded by using the maximum of the oversampled sequence, and that the oversampled inverse Fourier transform can be used as a reliable and fast method to compute the peak power of OFDM sequences.
we have introduced new results on the peak-to-mean ratio for uncoded OFDM systems and new results for the peak power of coded OFDM systems.

the oversampled inverse FFT method is a good candidate for peak power computation for uncoded systems, whereas the minimum distance decoding method is a good alternative for coded systems, and both methods have the same complexity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for uncoded OFDM, the oversampled inverse FFT is more efficient than minimum distance decoding for computing the peak envelope power of OFDM, and that the oversampled inverse Fourier transform is a viable option for computing the peak power of OFDM with coded modulation.

the peak power of OFDM can be accurately predicted from the oversampled discrete-time sequence, and that this sequence can be obtained from the discrete-time sequence with a small number of samples per subcarrier.
oversampling of the OFDM signal by an integer factor of 2 or more can significantly reduce the peak power of the signal, and thus reduce the impact of the nonlinearity.
